questions.q: In LIKE, what does the % wildcard match?
questions.explain: % matches zero or more characters; _ is the wildcard that matches exactly one character.

questions.q: WHERE Name LIKE 'Acme%' would match which value?
questions.explain: A trailing % anchors the match at the start of the string, so only values starting with 'Acme' match — not values with other text before it.

questions.q: What is the cleaner way to write WHERE BillingState = 'CA' OR BillingState = 'NY' OR BillingState = 'TX'?
questions.explain: IN checks membership against a list of values in one clause, equivalent to chaining multiple OR equality checks.

questions.q: Why are != and NOT LIKE called 'unselective' operators?
options: They require a GROUP BY clause to run
They are deprecated and will be removed from SOQL
They can only be used with numeric fields
They generally can't use an index efficiently, because 'everything except one value' usually matches most of a large table
questions.explain: An index helps when a filter narrows results down to a small fraction of a table; negative filters like != typically match most rows, so the optimizer can't use an index for them.

questions.q: WHERE NOT (StageName = 'Closed Lost') is most useful compared to StageName != 'Closed Lost' when:
options: The condition being negated is more complex than a single equality check, such as a parenthesized multi-part expression
You need to compare two numeric fields
The field being checked is a date field
You are filtering on a required field
questions.explain: For a simple single equality, != is simpler; NOT becomes valuable when you need to negate an entire complex, parenthesized expression at once.
